title: GPU variance signature authoring for model onboarding
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create a reproducible, versioned signature artifact (golden signature) that captures per-hardware variance for a new model during onboarding. Signatures should support comparing observed latency/throughput/percentile behavior across A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants and detect regressions relative to the pinned model+hw profile.
background: We currently publish per-GPU performance profiles based on point-benchmarks, but onboarding new models lacks an automated signature that encodes expected distributional behavior. This causes noisy triage, missed regressions when kernels change, and slow rollouts in Dedicated/Private where customers pin versions.
problem_statement: Onboarding workflow requires: a compact artifact that represents expected latency and token-cost distributions per hardware SKU; deterministic generation steps; an automated gate that fails rollouts if observed behavior deviates beyond thresholds. Existing docs enumerate metrics but not an authored signature format or workflow.
proposed_solution:
1) Define a JSONL signature format that includes: model version, input seed prompts, sequence length buckets, sample rates, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95), throughput (tokens/s) at representative batch sizes, memory headroom indicators, and kernel hint tags.
2) Implement a signature generator (python CLI) that runs a short stable micro-benchmark harness per device (A100/H100/L40S/MI300), uses deterministic seeds, and uploads signed artifacts to the hardware-profile registry.
3) Add a rollout gate in the pinning service that fetches the signature for target hw and compares live telemetry to the golden signature with configurable thresholds per metric.
4) Provide a small UI summary in Console (per-model HW signature card) and a diagnostics link to raw benchmark traces.
acceptance_criteria:
- Signature format documented in the onboarding spec (confluence).
- CLI can produce signatures for all four SKUs in a reproducible way (md5 of artifact reproducible across runs within noise tolerance).
- Automation jobs created in infra to run signature generation for model-onboard PRs.
- Pinning service rejects rollout when p95 latency regression > 15% OR throughput drop > 20% for a given hw profile.
- Console shows signature metadata and a link to the raw traces for any onboarded model.

risks: MI300 driver instability can cause signature generation to fail; we need retries and a driver-health check before capturing weak signals.
Reproducibility across cloud regions: thermal/scheduler differences may widen distributions requiring per-region baselines or loosened thresholds.
Overfitting signature thresholds may block legitimate kernel improvements; need an allow-list or staged-accept flow with manual review.
Storage footprint: preserving raw traces for every model+hw for long retention increases storage costs; mandate a 90-day hot retention + cold archive policy.
decisions: Use JSONL signature artifact (one beat per sample) so we can diff with standard tools and compress efficiently.
Canonicalize timestamps to UTC and include a reproducibility hash computed over canonical inputs to detect non-deterministic runs.
Default gate thresholds: p95 latency +15%, throughput -20%, memory headroom safety margin -10%.
Automate signature generation for PRs on the model-onboard repo; nightly full-generation runs for long-lived models.
